disposition_reason: This Matters Arising reanalysis asks whether apparent prestimulus tone decoding is explained by sequence statistics and biased classifier confusions. The result is a scientific null interpretation, not an ordered prediction benchmark. Higher decoding, larger Bayes evidence for the null, or a smaller p-value cannot by itself surpass the same finding; replacing it with a tone-classification leaderboard would change the registered endpoint.

target.description: Test whether prestimulus feature-specific decoding exceeds empirical reordered-sequence and confusion-matrix theoretical nulls; sounds and omissions remain distinct.

dataset.description: The 2026 reanalysis reuses Demarchi2019 MEG release DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3268713, not a new recording cohort.

cohort.description: Author sound code requires four conditions for every mapped participant. The registration specifies 33 participants/132 recordings, but publication-vintage participant inclusion and the full manifest join were not independently authenticated here.

split.description: Paper describes stratified five-fold classification trained on random-block sounds, with testing across entropies. Pinned sound code instead uses KFold(5), 0-0.32 s training and -0.666-0.666 s testing; historical producer/version parity remains unresolved.

inputs.description: MEG sensor data, sound/omission event identities and four entropy conditions, with segment reordering and transition/confusion matrices defining the controls.

preprocessing.description: Paper specifies provided 100 Hz, 1-30 Hz data; pinned sound code additionally filters 0.1-30 Hz and removes selected trigger events plus successors. Exact publication execution must be pinned for reconstruction.

metric.description: Tone accuracy is correct predictions divided by tested trials at each train/test time. Scientific assessment compares original and null maps and entropy correlations; 0.25 alone is not a valid prestimulus null.

aggregation.description: Author code averages fold accuracy within participants; R consumes participant matrices for group means, correlations and cluster/Bayesian inference. Time cells are not independent subjects.

comparison.primary_metric: No ordered same-task improvement endpoint established

published_baseline.description: No ordered numerical baseline represents the paper's negative scientific conclusion. Its accuracy, null contrasts and Bayes/cluster evidence cannot be reduced to a reward for a preferred conclusion.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: A reconstructed descriptive result is a calibration reference, not an improvement comparator.

minimum_effect.rationale: No scientifically justified scalar improvement direction exists for this registered finding; a larger effect or smaller p-value is not automatically better.

uncertainty.method: No improvement hypothesis is admitted. Preserve the source inferential analysis for reproduction.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant for paired group inference; trial order and shared samples remain dependent.
uncertainty.rationale: Valid uncertainty does not turn confirmation of a descriptive or null claim into an ordered performance contest.

paper_win_requires: No same-task improvement win is admitted for confirming or strengthening this negative finding.
Retain the original empirical/theoretical controls; higher tone accuracy alone does not demonstrate anticipatory neural information.
A new classifier benchmark or corrected time/split/null protocol must be separately labelled as an extension with its own objective; numerical parity remains calibration.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison has been verified; reproducing this finding establishes neither a paper win nor SOTA.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive: Original null-claim reconstruction is retained; no justified scalar improvement objective is available for the same scientific task.
episode.candidate_freeze: No candidate improvement episode is admitted. Preserve frozen historical reconstruction outputs separately.
episode.final_evaluation: Do not award surpass-source-paper success for this disposition. A separately approved replacement must supply its own original task and source baseline.
episode.baseline_policy: Historical reference agreement remains calibration only. Authored extensions and local analytical baselines cannot substitute for the source-paper result.

blocking_issues: Original scientific endpoint lacks a defensible direction in which a method can surpass the finding.
Paper versus pinned code differ in cross-validation wording and time-window implementation; a corrected profile cannot silently stand in for the paper.
Publication-vintage complete participant/file join remains unqualified.
A replacement must identify a source-reported ordered prediction task; stronger null evidence or sensitivity alone is not one.

legacy.notes: Retain full temporal-generalization matrices, empirical/theoretical nulls, group inference and historical/source reconciliation. corrected_methods_v1 and sensitivity/power studies remain methodological extensions, never paper-win substitutions.
